name: Guiñote
description: Guiñote is a Tute variant for 2 to 4 players from Aragón, Navarra and Castilla. It uses the same 40-card Spanish deck and point-trick structure as Tute, but the jack and horse swap rank and point values; singing (cantes) uses king and jack; multiple 20s or 40s may be sung after a trick; and the winner of the last trick deals next.

history.origins: Guiñote is a regional Tute variant played in Aragón, Navarra and part of Castilla. The name distinguishes it from standard Tute.
timeline: 20th century: documented as regional variant in Aragón, Navarra and Castilla.

setup.deck: Standard Spanish 40-card pack: four suits (Oros, Copas, Espadas, Bastos), ranks Ace down to Two. In Guiñote the jack (sota) ranks above the horse (caballo) and is worth 3 points; the horse is worth 2. Same pack as Tute.
setup.dealing: The first dealer is chosen at random. In Guiñote the winner of the last trick deals the next hand; if a hand ends by claim the winner of the game deals next.

rules.objective: Win tricks containing high-value cards and score points from card values, singing (king and jack of same suit for 20 or 40 points), and the last trick (10 points). The team or player with more points wins the deal; in match play the side that wins more deals wins.
rules.gameplay: Dealer deals all 40 cards (e.g. 10 each in the four-player game), one at a time face down; the last card is turned for trump. Player to dealer's right leads. Players must follow suit and, when possible, beat the highest card so far in the trick; if unable to follow suit they must trump and overtake if able. Trick winner leads next. After winning a trick a player may sing one or more 20s or 40s (king and jack of same suit) before leading. When all cards are played, points in tricks, singing, and last trick are counted; higher total wins the deal.
keyRules: Use 40-card Spanish deck; in Guiñote jack ranks above horse and is worth 3 points, horse 2.
Trump determined by turned card; follow suit and overtake when possible; must trump if cannot follow.
Sing 20 (king and jack of non-trump suit) or 40 (king and jack of trumps) after winning a trick; 40 must be declared before 20; multiple declarations allowed after one trick in Guiñote.
No tute (four kings or four horses) validity in Guiñote. Winner of last trick deals next hand.

strategy.basic: Lead low cards to force opponents to spend high cards; save trumps for key tricks; sing 40 before 20 when you have both.
strategy.intermediate: Count points and track which high cards have been played; time your trumps to win tricks that contain point cards.
strategy.advanced: Coordinate with partner in four-player; plan singing order to maximize points; use knowledge of remaining cards in the final tricks.
tips: Fix the exact local variant before play so edge cases are clear.

variations.description: In Guiñote jack ranks above horse and is worth 3 points (horse 2); singing uses king and jack (not king and horse); multiple 20s or 40s may be sung after one trick; tute (four kings or four horses) is not valid; winner of last trick deals next.

scoring.description: Count card points in won tricks (Ace 11, Three 10, King 4, Jack 3, Horse 2), add 10 for last trick, add 20 or 40 for each sung combination. Higher total wins the deal.
scoring.winCondition: The team or player with more total points (cards in tricks, singing, and 10 for last trick) wins the deal. If tied, the side that won the last trick wins.
